kjv: Ye shall not eat of every tree
mine: You must not eat from any tree
note: Hebrew lo' tokhlu mikkol 'ets means "you shall eat from no tree"; the KJV wording can be read as "not from all (only some) trees," which blunts the serpent's distortion.

Hebrew ke'lohim can be "like God" or "like gods/divine beings"; since 'elohim in the same verse is God, and 3:22 says "like one of us," either is possible, but the KJV chooses the plural. Context: like God (medium confidence). The first 'elohim in the verse is God; 3:22 'like one of us' confirms the knowledge is divine knowledge.

Hebrew hu' (masculine) refers to zera' "offspring"; the KJV's "it" treats the offspring collectively while "his heel" in the same verse is personal. The verb shuph is better "strike/crush" than "bruise." Traditionally read messianically.

kjv: cursed is the ground for thy sake
mine: cursed is the ground because of you
note: Hebrew ba'avurekha means "on account of you"; modern "for thy sake" suggests "for your benefit."
